headline.text: Pirkanmaa's crude curative treatment share of 31.9% exceeds the 27.0% national level, yet the county does not monitor whether its stated pathway target times are met.

details.text: Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several treatments, Pirkanmaa's crude shares are 31.9% (95% CI 29.4–34.6; n=400/1253) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally for curative, 36.2% (95% CI 33.5–38.9; n=453/1253) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) for life-prolonging, and 45.0% (95% CI 42.3–47.8; n=564/1253) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) for symptomatic treatment, with each 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

While treatment categories overlap, Pirkanmaa's crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—which mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—is 17.9% (95% CI 15.8–20.1; n=224/1253) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, and its crude MDT recording share is 37.4% (95% CI 34.8–40.1; n=469/1253) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with each 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

In Pirkanmaa's regional pathway document, referral handling in 1–2 working days, invitations in 3–4 working days, CT most often within a week, and bronchoscopy results in 3–5 days are unmonitored targets rather than commitments, and no diagnostic-phase contact person is named.

Under the Health Care Act there is no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion, while preliminary, unpublished national figures average 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark, across 56 patient, 41 primary-care, and 58 specialist-care days.

headline.text: Pirkanmaa's crude shares are not age-adjusted and cannot be stage-adjusted, though its low crude no-treatment-record share is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording as an inference.

details.text: County shares have distinct limitations: they are not age-adjusted—age-adjusted values exist only from Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex, digitised from a figure at about ±0.5 percentage points with national reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women—and, separately, they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

Because Pirkanmaa's crude 17.9% (95% CI 15.8–20.1; n=224/1253) no-treatment-record share has a 95% confidence interval below the 27.5% (4089/14873) national value, this is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording as an inference, not a finding, whereas a journal article's about 90% HILMO match covers diagnosis concordance only and HILMO MDT codes measure direct-contact recording practice, not care.

Primary care visits are not included in the report's data and occupational health is not mentioned at all, while public data do not capture symptom onset, referral dates, imaging waits (showing only that about 20% of diagnoses rest on clinical findings such as imaging alone), or when specialist visits (recorded for 93.6% within 12 months) or treatments occur.

headline.text: The team recommends that Pirkanmaa report THL 21/2016 access times with handover alerts, standardize referral templates with a named diagnostic contact, and publish county recording completeness.

details.text: Because regional pathway documents do not report whether stated target times are met and Finland lacks a unified national system monitoring access to care, the team recommends reporting access times from referral to first specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start using THL guidance 21/2016 definitions (covering 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers.

Supported by mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower specialist urgency rating while occupational health gets patients to specialist care faster, and because regional pathway documents name no diagnostic-phase contact person, the team recommends a standard referral template, referring persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray for pulmonologist assessment, and naming a diagnostic contact person.

The team recommends these local steps while national plans proceed: the STM roadmap plans standardised referral criteria (measure 2.5.2), pathway access times (measure 3.1.2), and named care-coordinator guidance (measure 1.2.3) by 2026–2028 (with county coordinator adoption by 2029–2031), and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because lung cancer data collection is incomplete and stage is missing for about 48% of patients, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding—reading gaps as data-quality signals first—while the STM roadmap plans a national quality registry at 90% coverage under measure 3.2.1 (decree updated by 2026–2028, reporting by 2029–2031).

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact.
